title: Commissioners' Meeting 04/14/25
tldr: With Vice-Chairman Dalton absent, the Board approved a consent agenda that included two proclamations, a $626,000 Library Foundation-funded amphitheater roof budget and a Duraline copier contract at $4,357.39 per month. It approved up to $9,000 to keep the Probation Parole office in its leased space month to month after the landlord raised the rent. The Manager gave updates on Hurricane Helene debris removal, the recent wildfires, capital planning for emergency services, and a state review delaying the Brevard High School roof project. The Chairman directed staff to write state officials asking for faster review of that project. The Board also met in closed session on a potential economic development project.

keyVotes.description: Approved consent agenda, including the $626,000 Library amphitheater roof budget and a $4,357.39/month Duraline copier contract
keyVotes.background: The consent agenda adopted Proclamation #13-2025 (National Day of Prayer, May 1) and Proclamation #14-2025 (Public Service Recognition Week, May 4–10). It also approved grant-funded out-of-state travel for two public health staff to present at the NACCHO360 Conference, and a $626,000 project budget for a Library Amphitheater roof fully funded by the Library Foundation. It also approved a Duraline copier contract at $4,357.39 per month, the lowest of three bids, which adds three aging plotters to the agreement.

keyVotes.description: Approved up to $9,000 for month-to-month Probation Parole office lease costs
keyVotes.background: The County has provided leased space for Probation Parole off Caldwell Street for over 25 years. The lease expired February 28, 2024 and now runs month to month, and the lessor has asked for $500/month more in rent plus utility costs. The Manager requested $6,000 for a year of increased rent and $3,000 toward utilities while the County works with NCDAC on an interim location. State law (N.C.G.S. §15-209) requires counties to provide suitable space, and the new courthouse will eventually house the office.
keyVotes.discussion: McCall asked how much notice would be needed to vacate, and the Manager said it could be very little. Chapman asked about space needs, and the Manager said five offices are required. McKelvey suggested a 12-month lease and said the owner had implied one might be possible; the Manager said she would relay this to NCDAC, which handles lease negotiations. McCall asked whether the County could place the office in County space that does not meet NCDAC criteria. The Manager said the statute supports offering reasonable space but NCDAC has rejected prior alternatives.

keyVotes.description: Entered closed session after a 10-minute recess to discuss economic development (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
keyVotes.background: The closed session concerned matters relating to the location or expansion of industries or other businesses. The Transylvania Economic Alliance Executive Director attended. The Board received information on a potential economic development project and directed staff on how to proceed.
Procedural motion to return to open session.
The minutes are sealed until opening them would not frustrate the purpose of the closed session.

topics.text: Asked whether FEMA had addressed all storm damage assistance applications.
Expressed concern about residents reporting that FEMA refused to inspect their properties, and said she has been directing residents to their federal representatives.
Asked about the locations of the two proposed communication towers.
Asked how much notice would be required to vacate the Probation Parole office.
Asked whether the County could place Probation Parole in County space that does not fully meet NCDAC criteria.
Questioned whether a similar NCDPI review was required for the Rosman roof project, suggesting the BHS review request may be atypical.
Expressed frustration with the BHS project delay and hoped state leaders would intervene.
Thanked the County Manager for her testimony in Washington, D.C. and her leadership during Hurricane Helene and the wildfires.
Reported visiting the Hannah Ford Road area, where he met the river debris removal contractor, and praised its work as potentially saving the County millions in future damages.
Noted that drones were mapping the river for cleanup and that a large mulching operation was processing collected debris.
Asked about the office space needs of Probation Parole.
Reported observing the BHS project site and noted that work had paused.
Announced that Transylvania County will host the District 16 NCACC meeting on April 22, where Cameron Sexton will be honored.
Asked for thoughts and prayers for Representative Mike Clampitt, who announced serious health issues.
Suggested a 12-month lease for the Probation Parole office and said the property owner had recently implied such a lease might be possible.
Said the Probation Parole lease situation aligns with written NCDAC correspondence and that a change in the owner's position would be positive.
Thanked staff for their efforts and acknowledged the County's responsibility to provide required office space within its means.
With Board support, directed staff to draft a letter to the State Superintendent and the state legislative delegation seeking expedited review of the BHS project.
Thanked the agencies and individuals involved in the wildfire response and asked that the Manager's presentation slides be posted to the County website.
Commended law enforcement, including an off-duty deputy, for their response to a high-speed tractor trailer incident.
Praised the County Manager's leadership and statewide reputation.

externalRoles: National Association of Counties (NACo) Rural Advocacy Committee

publicComments.speaker: Bruce Gleasman
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern that the County budget has grown 64% since 2015 while the population grew 2%. Urged wiser spending and consideration of taxpayers, and suggested aiming for the lowest tax rate in North Carolina. He began to mention an alternative courthouse site as his time ended.

publicComments.speaker: Lisa Presnell
publicComments.summary: Praised the Marine Corps JROTC program in Transylvania County Schools and noted that it has grown enough to qualify for federal funding. Highlighted cadets' success at a regional competition and a full college scholarship, and encouraged continued support.

publicComments.speaker: Sarah Carson
publicComments.summary: A Rosman High School teacher who invited the Board to a Trout in the Classroom community learning expo at Champion Park on April 25. She also raised concerns that Commissioner Chapman's social media comments were inappropriate for a public official.

publicComments.speaker: Gerald Yunker
publicComments.summary: Asked the Board to consider food access when planning the new courthouse, suggesting an on-site food option if it is located farther from restaurants.

publicComments.speaker: Ashley Hart
publicComments.summary: Commended the Connestee Fire Department for its response to the Table Rock Fire and asked the Board to consider inviting its members to a future meeting for formal recognition.

followUps.description: Draft a letter to the State Superintendent of Public Instruction and the County's state legislative delegation requesting expedited NCDPI review of the BHS Scope #1 roof project.
Relay to NCDAC that the Probation Parole property owner may be open to a 12-month lease, as NCDAC handles lease negotiations.
Post the Manager's wildfire presentation slides showing the fire's progression and impact to the County website.
